# CM5 R0: finite homological models and the rank-one bar reduction (040)

## Disposition

The finite-free replacement and tensor-power finite-generation
mechanisms are now kernel-checked, as is induction over all positive
Eilenberg–Mac Lane stages from the actual additive bar base. This
does not assert the remaining rank-one bar homology computation.

Parent PR #3850 is protected at merge
60afab132850f9c6f09dcd3d522d9f2f88db1780.

## Finite subcomplex

Let C be any nonnegative integral chain complex with finitely
generated homology. For a finite submodule V contained in the range
of a linear map, choose finitely many generators of V and lift them.
The span of the lifts is finite and maps onto V.

In each degree choose a finite submodule of the cycles mapping
onto homology. Write L_n for its image in C_n. Define F_0=L_0.
Given F_n, the intersection of F_n with the range of the next
differential is finite by Noetherianity of finite integer modules.
Choose a finite lift U of this intersection into C_(n+1).
Put F_(n+1)=L_(n+1)+U. The exact equality is

$$
d(F_{n+1})=F_n\cap\mathrm{im}(d:C_{n+1}\to C_n).
$$

Thus these actual submodules form a complex. Its inclusion into C
is surjective on homology by the selected cycle representatives
and injective by the boundary-lifting equality. All degrees are
handled by one recursion, not by independent incompatible truncations.

If the original chain terms are free, the finite subcomplex terms
are finite and torsion-free, hence finite free over the integers.
Both complexes are bounded below and degreewise projective.
The Mathlib projective-complex quasi-isomorphism criterion supplies
a chain homotopy equivalence. This bypasses the infinite-rank
subgroup freeness/splitting step in the source reconstruction 030.

## 43. Lemma K: the last local-to-global assembly

The desired group is not the Sha group itself. The coefficient lattice is $T=\mathbb Z_\ell(E+1)$ and its complementary discrete Tate dual is $A=\mathbb Q_\ell/\mathbb Z_\ell(-E)$. The global Galois group here is unramified outside the finite primes $S$ above $\ell$. Lemma K seeks finiteness and a uniform logarithmic order bound on $H^2(G_{L,S},T)$.

SFinal explicitly takes three foundational inputs: PoitouTateDuality, LocalFinitenessK and LocalTateDualityK. They are not discharged by SFinal. Poitou–Tate identifies the kernel of the second-cohomology localization map with the dual of the first-cohomology Sha group; its cokernel is dual to the global invariants of $A$. Local Tate duality identifies the orders or lengths of local second cohomology with local invariants. The total-complex hypothesis eliminates real-place corrections, including at the prime two.

![Global second cohomology is bounded by the Sha length and local invariants, followed by numerical absorption](../assets/rh-a26-sfinal.svg)

Write $s$ for the global Sha length and $V$ for the length of second cohomology. Two short exact sequences with a common localization image give the length identity

$$
V+\mathrm{length}\,H^0(G_{L,S},A)
=s+\sum_{v\mid\ell}\mathrm{length}\,H^0(G_{L_v},A).
$$

## 42. Absorbing the enlargement cost into one universal exponent

SNum is the numerical join of the preceding conditional bounds. It is important that the field enlargement is measured in the variables that enter the homological estimate, rather than by the discriminant alone.

Write $n=[L:\mathbb Q]$, $D=|\mathrm{disc}(L)|$ and $x=2En$. SLayer gives $d\le16En=8x$, $n'=dn\le4x^2$ and $w\le2n'$. Thus $2En'\le8x^2\le x^5$. Taking logarithms of the discriminant bound yields

$$
\log(2D')\le \log 2+d\log D+n'\log w
\le73x^4\log(2D)\le x^{11}\log(2D).
$$

The arithmetic generator count can also be bounded independently. Minkowski gives an integral ideal of norm at most $\sqrt{D'}$ in every ideal class (the Minkowski constant is at most one). Ideals inject into ordered positive integer tuples of length $n'$ with product their norm: order the primes above each rational prime, assign the corresponding residue-degree-weighted exponents to the coordinates, and pad unused coordinates. Summing recursively and using the harmonic sum bound gives at most $X(1+\log X)^{n'-1}$ tuples of product at most $X$. Consequently the class number logarithm is at most $(\log D')/2+n'\log(1+(\log D')/2)$ and the generator parameter satisfies $G\le2n'+4n'\log(2D')+2$.

Set $u=2En'$ and $Y=\log(2D')$. The loss parameters obey $b\le u+2u^2$, $c,v,\log\ell\le u$, and $G\le u+2uY+2\le6uY$. Since $u\ge2$ and $Y\ge1/2$, the arithmetic contribution satisfies

$$
\Delta\log\ell=((b+v)G+c+v)\log\ell\le19u^4Y\le u^9Y.
$$

# CM5 R0: finite-lattice Breen–Deligne extension (039)

## Disposition

The extension from a degreewise finite polynomial resolution on finite
free integer lattices to all abelian groups is kernel-checked. This
is a reduction of the remaining existence problem, not a construction
of an inhabitant of the finite-lattice resolution type.

The input is the explicit LatticeBD structure in the required lifted
coefficient universe. The output LatticeBD.toUniversalBD supplies the
actual natural augmentation and differentials, their identities,
epimorphic augmentation and categorical exactness in every degree.

The canonical comparison is the existing protected endpoint of 038:
canonicalUnit_allShifts_of_LatticeBD is obtained by applying that
endpoint to the constructed UniversalBD package. Parent PR #3845
merged at 5dd36e28545e13e7b654454ad047911e21a824f3.

## Construction

For a polynomial functor

$$
P(A)=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{k}\mathbb Z[A^{r_j}],
$$

a natural map on finite free lattices extends uniquely to all
modules. Each tuple is the image of the generic tuple in the
appropriate finite free lattice. The formula applies the target
functor to this tuple map and the value on the generic tuple.
Naturality and the restriction identity are checked on free
generators. Injectivity of restriction implies that the augmentation
and differential identities on the lattices extend to the whole
module category.

Every polynomial element of an arbitrary free module involves a
finite union of finite supports of basis vectors. A finite-coordinate
retraction fixes the element. Exactness on finite free modules
therefore gives exactness on free modules of arbitrary rank.

For an arbitrary surjection of modules, form the actual equal-image

## Disposition

transport for a supplied universal finite-type Breen–Deligne package.
The existence of the package itself is not yet kernel-proved. No
MATHCERT claim, protected admission claim, circle calculation, or
biduality claim follows from this receipt.

The input is Theorem 4.10 of Peter Scholze, *Lectures on Condensed
Mathematics*, arXiv:2605.03658v1 (5 May 2026), material jointly developed
with Dustin Clausen: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03658v1 .
Theorem 4.10 supplies a natural exact augmented resolution of the
identity on abelian groups by finite sums of free finite-power functors.
We use that existence theorem, not a newly postulated Ext vanishing.
In Lean, the explicit input UniversalBD consists of these natural maps,
finite arities, augmentation, and exactness in the functor category.
An inhabitant of UniversalBD has not been constructed internally.

zero follows from surjectivity of precomposition with projection;
positive degrees follow by retract from the free relative real product.
